ask: one-pager for Tesco's category buyer about our compostable packaging, to send ahead of the call
notes: Format (one-pager), meeting kind (sent to read) and the product facts are given. A4 for a UK company is set without asking. Quick track fits a single page.
message:
**Goal:** a one-page A4 sheet that a Tesco category buyer reads before your call, and that leaves them willing to test Leafwrap compostable film.

**Found:**
- Product facts from `product.md`: home-compostable produce film, breaks down in 26 weeks in a home bin, TUV OK compost HOME certified, price parity with PET film over 40 tonnes a year.
- Customers named in `product.md`: Riverford (since 2024) and Abel & Cole (trial).
- Format from your ask: a one-pager, sent ahead of the call. It is UK, so A4 portrait.
- Lands in: `decks/tesco-20261126/out/` as an HTML page and a PDF to attach to your email.
- For: Tesco's category buyer, before the call. I will only claim what `product.md` says, and nothing about Tesco unless a source link backs it.

**Track:** quick, because one page to read ahead of a call needs only HTML and a PDF. No PowerPoint is made.

Still open after reading your files: what the page should get the buyer to do, and which customers we may name.

**Done means:**
- One A4 page that asks the buyer for a trial of Leafwrap film.
- `deck.html` and `deck.pdf` are in `out/` and open.
- Every line cites `product.md` or a source link.
- The deck check prints PASS on every check.
- Every review finding is fixed or left with a reason.

The full brief, with defaults for everything else, is in `loop-runs/product-deck-loop-20261126-035330/brief.md`. Web search is not available in this session, so research uses only your file.

About 15 minutes and 3 helper agents, within a budget of 90 minutes.

1. What should the buyer believe or do after reading it?
   Recommended: a pitch. Their need for packaging that composts at home, how Leafwrap meets it, proof, and a request for a trial run. Other options: an outside-in view of the shift away from plastic film, or a plan for a first trial in one produce line.
   Why it matters: the goal decides the page's headline and what goes in each block.

2. May we name Riverford and Abel & Cole, and say Abel & Cole is a trial?
   Recommended: name Riverford, and write "in trial with another UK organic box retailer" for Abel & Cole.
   Why it matters: a customer named without permission can cost trust, and a trial may be confidential.

3. Who else will read it, and what do they care about?
   Recommended: only the buyer, who may forward it to a packaging technologist. The page stays short on price and long on the certificate.
   Why it matters: a forwarded page needs the certificate and test detail, and not just the commercial case.

4. What is the next step you want to ask for on the call?
   Recommended: a trial of one produce line, with a named contact from you.
   Why it matters: the closing block must say one clear next step, and I will not invent a contact name or a date.

5. Any look to follow, such as a logo or brand colours?
   Recommended: plain, with Arial, dark text on white and one dark green accent.
   Why it matters: with no brand file, I will not guess your colours.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.
